reviewerDerivedProposition: A verbal SBAR handoff to the receiving home health nurse must transmit the transition-critical continuity risks: LEP/interpreter dependence (A), rivaroxaban 10 mg x35d with adherence and bleeding surveillance (B), the transient creatinine rise that returned to baseline in a client on a renally cleared anticoagulant (C), living alone in a second-floor walk-up once the son leaves with home-safety/stair assessment outstanding (D), and confirmed equipment/functional status/follow-up appointment/son-as-phone-contact (F). A personal beverage preference is not transition-safety information (E excluded).
requiredFacts: A: Mandarin primary language, cannot reliably discuss medications or read English documents - ESTABLISHED at baseline_record.
B: rivaroxaban 10 mg PO daily x35 days ordered - baseline_record; adherence uncertainty - stage_pod1 barrier list.

C: 'trended up transiently AND returned to baseline' requires the full series cr 1.4/eGFR38 (baseline) -> 1.5/eGFR36 (pod1) -> 1.4/eGFR39 (pod2) -> 1.3/eGFR42 (pod3). The return-to-baseline conjunct is ONLY true at stage_pod3.
D: lives alone, second-floor walk-up, son 2 h away - baseline; 'after the son leaves' (son available discharge day +1 only) - stage_pod2.

F: 'follow-up appointment ... confirmed' is false at pod1 ('no confirmed follow-up appointment') and still unconfirmed at pod2; the surgeon's office confirmation and son-as-contact confirmation occur ONLY at stage_pod3.
disclosureEvidence: stage_pod3 exhibit pod3_update states verbatim: 'The nurse calls the receiving home health nurse using SBAR and communicates language needs, the need for an interpreter for teaching, social situation, functional status, equipment, rivaroxaban dose/duration and adherence concerns, renal-function trend, bleeding surveillance, son's role as the communication contact, and the confirmed follow-up appointment.'
